title: Selling Property in Türkiye & Repatriating Funds Abroad Legally
seoTitle: Selling Property in Türkiye & Repatriating Funds Legally
metaDescription: Understand Turkish Tapu sale documents, compliant SWIFT repatriation, the 5-year capital gains exemption, and the 3-year citizenship lock.
quickAnswer: Foreign owners selling real estate in Türkiye need a clear Tapu title deed, municipal property tax clearance, valid DASK earthquake insurance, and a licensed appraisal when selling to another foreigner. Proceeds can be transferred abroad legally via SWIFT under [Central Bank (TCMB) foreign exchange rules](https://www.tcmb.gov.tr/wps/wcm/connect/TR/TCMB+TR/Main+Menu/Banka+Hakkinda/Mevzuat/Kambiyo/) once taxes are settled, and properties held over 5 years qualify for capital gains exemption.

body.text: Exiting a Turkish real estate investment smoothly requires coordinating land registry paperwork, municipal tax clearance, and international banking compliance in the right order. At [Itinerary of Türkiye](https://itineraryofturkiye.com/)—an independent, client-paid, flat-fee travel, business, and medical travel advisory run by its two founders in Türkiye ("Paid by our clients. Independent of provider commissions.")—we arrange structured in-country visits for property owners returning to handle closings. Important boundary: Itinerary of Türkiye coordinates visits, scheduling, and independent introductions only; real estate conveyancing, Tapu filings, tax declarations, and cross-border legal opinions belong strictly to licensed Turkish attorneys, SMMM accountants, and official authorities.
What documents and tax clearances are required to sell Turkish real estate?

To transfer ownership at the Land Registry Office (Tapu Müdürlüğü), sellers must present the original title deed (Tapu), passport with notarized Turkish translation, Turkish tax number, a municipal Rayiç Bedel (fair value) and "no tax debt" (borcu yoktur) certificate, and an active DASK mandatory earthquake insurance policy.

Under [TKGM Foreign Affairs Department](https://www.tkgm.gov.tr/yabanci-isler-dairesi-baskanligi) procedures and [Invest in Türkiye's land registry guidelines](https://www.invest.gov.tr/en/investmentguide/pages/acquiring-property-and-citizenship.aspx), a sworn interpreter must attend the Tapu signing if either party does not speak Turkish. If the buyer is also a foreign national, a licensed SPK real estate valuation report is mandatory under [TKGM valuation rules](https://www.tkgm.gov.tr/antalya-bm/haberler/yabanciya-konut-satisinda-degerleme-zorunlugu), and foreign buyers must complete a Foreign Currency Purchase Certificate (Döviz Alım Belgesi, DAB) through a Turkish bank before closing. Standard Tapu transfer fee (Tapu Harcı) totals 4% of the declared sale price, typically split 2% each unless otherwise agreed.

body.text: How do you transfer sale proceeds abroad cleanly via SWIFT with bank compliance?

Under the [Central Bank of the Republic of Türkiye (TCMB) foreign exchange legislation](https://www.tcmb.gov.tr/wps/wcm/connect/TR/TCMB+TR/Main+Menu/Banka+Hakkinda/Mevzuat/Kambiyo/), foreign nationals may freely transfer real estate sale proceeds abroad through authorized Turkish banks via SWIFT once applicable taxes and obligations are satisfied. Clean bank compliance depends entirely on declaring the true sale price on the Tapu and routing the buyer's payment directly into your Turkish bank account.

Declaring the full, accurate sale price on the title deed is essential because both Turkish sending banks and foreign receiving banks conduct thorough source-of-funds reviews. When your Turkish bank converts TRY proceeds into USD, EUR, or GBP and initiates a SWIFT transfer, its compliance team matches the transfer amount directly against the signed Tapu sale price, the buyer's bank transfer receipt (dekont), and your sales contract. Unrecorded payments outside the Tapu figure cannot be verified for international clearance.
When does the 5-year capital gains exemption apply?

Under Article Mükerrer 80 of Income Tax Law No. 193 and the [Revenue Administration (GİB) Real Estate Capital Gains Guide](https://www.gib.gov.tr/vergi-konulari/1_bireysel/7_diger_kazanc_ve_iratlar/7), individual owners who hold a property for more than five full calendar years from the Tapu registration date are exempt from Turkish capital gains tax (Değer Artışı Kazancı) upon sale.

If you sell before completing five full years of ownership, you must calculate the inflation-adjusted gain using the Producer Price Index (Yİ-ÜFE) method published by the [Revenue Administration (GİB)](https://www.gib.gov.tr/mevzuat/kanun/433) and file an annual income tax return in March of the following year. Inherited properties and properties acquired without consideration are generally outside this 5-year tax rule, while frequent buying and selling can be classified as commercial trading income by an SMMM accountant or tax office.
What rules apply if you obtained citizenship through the property (3-year lock)?

Properties purchased for Turkish Citizenship by Investment carry a mandatory 3-year non-sale annotation (satılamaz şerhi) recorded on the title deed under [Invest in Türkiye](https://www.invest.gov.tr/en/investmentguide/pages/acquiring-property-and-citizenship.aspx) and [NVI citizenship rules](https://www.nvi.gov.tr/turk-vatandasliginin-kazanilmasi). You cannot legally sell the property until three full years have elapsed from the date the annotation was entered on the Tapu.

Once the 3-year holding period expires, you or your attorney can request removal of the annotation at the Land Registry Office and proceed with a standard sale without affecting your acquired Turkish citizenship. Lifting the 3-year citizenship lock does not waive the separate 5-year capital gains tax threshold: selling between year three and year five still requires capital gains tax review on the inflation-adjusted profit. If you are timing an off-season closing trip to Istanbul or the coast, our [Türkiye winter travel guide](https://itineraryofturkiye.com/blog/turkey-in-winter-premium-travel-guide) outlines quieter travel windows and logistics.
Seller Compliance Checklist Before Listing or Closing

items: Verify your exact Tapu registration date to confirm whether the 5-year capital gains exemption or 3-year citizenship lock applies.
Clear all municipal Emlak Vergisi, homeowners association (aidat), and utility balances prior to your Tapu appointment.
Confirm your Turkish bank account is active and pre-notify your branch relationship manager of the incoming sale proceeds and planned SWIFT transfer.
Declare the full, actual purchase price on the Tapu and receive all buyer funds via traceable bank transfer (Tapu Takas or bank-to-bank transfer).
Engage a licensed SMMM accountant to verify whether a March capital gains return is required after closing.

faq.q: Do I need to travel to Türkiye in person to sell my property?
faq.a: No. You can grant a specific Power of Attorney (Vekâletname) to a licensed Turkish attorney either at a Turkish notary in Türkiye or through a Turkish Consulate abroad (or apostilled local notary, depending on jurisdiction).

faq.q: What is Tapu Takas and should foreign sellers use it?
faq.a: Tapu Takas is an official escrow-style settlement system operated with Takasbank and TKGM that holds the buyer's funds securely and releases them to the seller simultaneously upon title deed transfer.

faq.q: Can the buyer pay me directly into my foreign bank account abroad?
faq.a: Cross-border direct settlement complicates Turkish Tapu proof-of-payment rules—especially when a foreign buyer needs a Turkish bank DAB—and can delay compliance review at your home bank. Routing funds transparently through a Turkish bank account is standard practice.

faq.q: Will I owe tax in my home country when I transfer the funds?
faq.a: Possibly. Even if your sale is exempt in Türkiye after 5 years, your country of tax residence may tax worldwide capital gains subject to any applicable double taxation treaty. Consult a qualified tax advisor in both jurisdictions.

faq.q: How long does a SWIFT transfer from a Turkish bank usually take?
faq.a: Once the Turkish bank's compliance team approves the Tapu deed and transfer receipts, international SWIFT transfers in USD, EUR, or GBP typically settle in 1 to 3 business days.

faq.q: Can I sell a citizenship property back to the original developer after 3 years?
faq.a: Wait until the 3-year annotation is formally lifted and have a licensed Turkish attorney review current citizenship regulations before selling back to the original seller or developer, as specific regulatory restrictions apply to repeat transactions.
